This was a "new thought" to me, and fell with overwhelming force. I lived over again the days of little district schools in Massachusetts. Those, at the time, I had regarded as sorely lamentable; but this system for the children of very poor, unfortunate, or unworthy parents seemed too unbearable. I think it was the first Monday in December 1851, when I classed my school and commanced teaching it.
